title: Payment Arrangement Reinstatement and Renegotiation Limits
content:
# Payment Arrangement Reinstatement and Renegotiation Limits

Two later changes are possible on some kinds of Payment Arrangement: putting a defaulted plan back into force (reinstatement) and changing the installment count of an active plan for a change in the customer's circumstances (renegotiation). The limits for each kind are:

| Arrangement kind | Reinstatements allowed | Days after the default to request reinstatement | Share of all missed installments to be paid before reinstatement | Renegotiations allowed | Ceiling on total installments after renegotiation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | 1 | 30 | 100% | 1 | 9 |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | 1 | 30 | 100% | 1 | 18 |
| Winter Protection Plan | 1 | 30 | 100% | 0 | 0 |
| Arrearage Management Program | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |

## Notes to the table

1. A reinstatement window of 0 days and a share of 0% mean the kind offers no reinstatement.
2. A renegotiation ceiling of 0 means the kind offers no renegotiation.
3. Reinstatement is offered on three kinds — the Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, the Extended Deferred Payment Agreement and the Winter Protection Plan — once each. Renegotiation is offered on the two deferred payment agreements, once each.
4. The share of missed installments is a fraction of all installments recorded as missed on the plan; 100% means every missed installment.
